It has a Revolving Credit Facility (with L/C and swing line subfacilities) and a Term Facility with a delayed draw feature. Up to two Term Loans may be made, to the Company only, during an Availability Period ending six months after the Closing Date. Delayed-draw borrowings after the Closing Date are capped at $75,000,000. Term Loans cannot be reborrowed.

However, the TS requires the whole Term Loan Facility to be drawn on the Closing Date, while the CA adds a delayed-draw feature (up to $75m drawable within six months after closing). This flexibility favours the Borrowers and is paired with a new ticking fee (see A15). The CA also makes Term Loans to the Company only, where the TS spoke of the Borrowers generally; obligations remain joint and several, so this is a drafting point.

rows.ts_value: RC increases and/or new incremental term tranches, in minimums of $20M with $5M increments (or less if the Agent accepts). Cap: the Fixed Incremental Amount (the greater of $535M and 100% of Consolidated EBITDA, less all incrementals already incurred) plus unlimited amounts if pro forma secured debt/EBITDA is no more than 1.25x. Conditions and terms: no default or unmatured default when requested or when effective; incremental term maturity no earlier than facility termination (bridge exception); IED allowed on a pari passu ranking and security basis; TLB Provisions; no increase to the LC or Swingline sublimits without the Fronting Bank's or Swingline Lender's consent.

rows.ca_value: s.2.14 allows Revolving Credit Increases, Term Loan Increases (to the existing Term Facility or a prior Incremental Term Loan) and Incremental Term A and B Loans, up to the Incremental Available Amount. That amount is the Incremental Fixed Amount (the greater of 100% of pro forma Consolidated EBITDA and $535,000,000, less only amounts incurred in reliance on it and not reclassified) plus the Incremental Ratio Amount (unlimited if the pro forma Consolidated Secured Leverage Ratio is no more than 1.25:1.00). Minimum $20,000,000 (or all remaining availability, or less if the Agent accepts) with $5,000,000 multiples. Conditions at the Increase Effective Date: reps true in all material respects, no Default or Event of Default, and pro forma compliance with the s.7.12 financial covenants, each with Limited Condition Acquisition carve-outs. Incremental Term A/B Loans cannot mature earlier than, or have a shorter WAL than, the Term Facility, with a Permitted Bridge Indebtedness carve-out. IED may rank and be secured pari passu or junior. No increase to the L/C or Swing Line Sublimits without the L/C Issuer's or Swing Line Lender's consent.
rows.ca_quote: the greater of (i) 100% of Consolidated EBITDA for the Subject Period most recently ended for which financial statements have been delivered pursuant to Section 6.01(a) or (b) (as applicable), calculated on a pro forma basis, and (ii) $535,000,000
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Incremental Available Amount', 'Incremental Equivalent Debt', 'Incremental Fixed Amount', 'Incremental Ratio Amount' (PDF p.13); s.2.14(a)-(d) (PDF pp.38-40)
rows.explanation: The core capacity matches: a $535M / 100% EBITDA fixed amount plus unlimited capacity at secured leverage of 1.25x or less, with $20M/$5M minimums and sublimit consent protections. The terms differ in substance in both directions. In the Borrowers' favour, the CA adds increases to the existing term tranche, deducts from the fixed amount only usage in reliance on it (with automatic reclassification to the ratio basket; the TS deducted all prior Incremental Facilities), adds LCA carve-outs, tests the no-default condition only at effectiveness (the TS also tested at request) and allows junior-ranking IED where the TS required pari passu. In the lenders' favour, the CA adds a rep bring-down, pro forma financial covenant compliance and WAL tests that the TS did not state. On balance the Borrowers gain flexibility. All of the changes are customary, so the difference is minor.

rows.ts_value: $150,000,000 standby LC sublimit within the RC, covering performance and financial LCs, with financial LCs capped at $75,000,000. Bank of America issues as Fronting Bank. LCs can be issued from the Closing Date to the Maturity Date. If an FX recalculation pushes LC exposure above 105% of the $150M sublimit, the Borrowers must cash collateralise the amount needed to eliminate that excess.
rows.ts_quote: an amount equal to 105% of the sublimit of $150,000,000 for Letters of Credit, the Borrowers will cash collateralize Letters of Credit in the amount necessary to eliminate such excess.
rows.ts_location: PDF p.2 (Senior Credit Facility); PDF p.3 (105% cash collateral); PDF pp.5-6 (Availability - LC issuance to Maturity Date)
rows.ca_value: The Letter of Credit Sublimit is the lesser of the RC Facility and $150,000,000, and sits within the RC. Financial Letter of Credit Sublimit: $75,000,000. Letters of Credit are standby only. The L/C Issuer is Bank of America ($150,000,000 L/C Commitment under Schedule 2.01), plus up to three additional Lenders the Company may select. LCs can be issued until the Letter of Credit Expiration Date, seven days before the Maturity Date. Each LC must be at least the Dollar Equivalent of $1,000,000 (unless otherwise agreed) and expire within twelve months unless the Required Revolving Lenders approve. Under s.2.05(d), if outstanding LCs exceed 105% of the sublimit 'as a result of fluctuations in exchange rates or for any other reason', the Borrowers must, within two Business Days, cash collateralise enough to bring the Outstanding Amount down to 100% of the sublimit.
rows.ca_quote: 105% of the Letter of Credit Sublimit then in effect, then, within two Business Days after receipt of such notice, the Borrowers shall Cash Collateralize L/C Obligations in an aggregate amount sufficient to reduce such Outstanding Amount as of such date of payment to an amount not to exceed 100%
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'L/C Issuer', 'Letter of Credit', 'Letter of Credit Expiration Date', 'Letter of Credit Sublimit' (PDF p.15); s.2.03(a) (PDF pp.27-28); s.2.05(d) (PDF p.34); Schedule 2.01 (PDF p.84)
rows.explanation: The $150M sublimit, the $75M financial LC cap, standby-only LCs and Bank of America as issuer match. The differences are: (1) the TS requires cash collateral only for the excess over 105% of the sublimit and only after an FX recalculation; the CA applies the 105% trigger to any cause and requires cash collateral down to 100%, so a breach costs the Borrowers up to $7.5M (5% of the sublimit) more in cash collateral; (2) issuance stops seven days before the Maturity Date, not at the Maturity Date; (3) the CA adds a $1M minimum LC amount and a twelve-month tenor cap. These favour the lenders. Against them, the CA lets the Company add up to three additional L/C Issuers, where the TS named only Bank of America, which favours the Borrowers. Overall this is a minor difference in the lenders' favour.

rows.ts_value: While any default continues, the margin on obligations rises by 2% a year. This is automatic for a principal payment default and otherwise applies only at the Required Lenders' request.

rows.ca_value: The Default Rate is the Base Rate plus the Base Rate Applicable Rate plus 2%. For Term SOFR Loans it is the applicable rate plus 2%, and for LC Fees the Applicable Rate plus 2%. Overdue principal bears the Default Rate automatically. Other overdue amounts bear it at the Required Lenders' request. While any Event of Default exists, all Obligations bear it at the Required Lenders' request after written notice to the Company. LC Fees bear it during an Event of Default at the Required Lenders' request.
rows.ca_quote: Upon the request of the Required Lenders and after written notice to the Company, while any Event of Default exists (other than as set forth in clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) above), the Borrowers shall pay interest on the principal amount of all outstanding Obligations hereunder
rows.ca_location: s.1.01 'Default Rate' (PDF p.9); s.2.08(b) (PDF p.35); s.2.03(h) (PDF p.31)
rows.explanation: The +2% step-up and the split between automatic (principal) and Required Lenders' request match. The CA narrows the TS mechanic, though. Under the TS, a principal payment default automatically raises the margin on all obligations. Under the CA, only the overdue principal bears the Default Rate automatically, and the step-up on all Obligations needs a Required Lenders' request and written notice to the Company while an Event of Default exists. The narrower trigger and added notice condition are a minor difference in the Borrowers' favour.
